warrant: Human ruling 2026-09-16 on PR #780 ('yeah switch to pointwise i think'): the copied driver already dumps the transformed array, and grading only its max and mean magnitude (the prior invariants policy) cannot separate a wrong sign, a swapped index or a wrong twiddle factor from a correct value when the aggregate is unchanged; pointwise on the array element by element catches it. transformed compares every element of the array the first forward transform produces under |candidate - reference| <= 1e-09 + 1e-09*|reference|, printed at 17 significant digits (1PE24.16, scale factor 1P) so the stream itself never floors the bound (references/pitfalls/output-precision-floors-the-bound.md). rtol is traced to the round-off of a double-precision cosine transform of N=1000: the mechanism floor is on the order of N times machine epsilon, 2.22e-13 here (eps=2.22e-16), and the bound sits 4,504x above it, real headroom for reordering across compilers, architectures and radix decomposition while still separating a fault: a wrong sign, a transposed axis or a wrong twiddle factor moves an element by an order-1 relative amount, six to nine orders of magnitude over the bound. atol is derived from the input's own scale rather than from the measured spread: ic/nominal is drawn from numpy's default_rng uniform on [0, 1), so max|input| <= 1, and atol = rtol * max|input| = 1e-09 ties the absolute floor for near-zero transformed elements to the same relative scale rtol already uses at the input's own magnitude, rather than an independently invented number. roundtrip-max-error is kept as a secondary invariant at its unchanged bound (atol 1e-09, rtol 0): its analytic value is exactly zero (references/pitfalls/residual-below-one-ulp.md), so it is graded as an OK/FAILED ceiling on the round-off remainder of the forward/inverse stages rather than folded into the pointwise set.
